# @zakkster/lite-delaunay

Version: 1.2.0

> Zero-GC 2D Delaunay triangulation. Pre-allocated arena, sweepline algorithm,
> half-edge mesh output. Built for per-frame use in games and simulations
> where `new Delaunator(coords)` every frame would cause GC stutter.
> As of 1.1.0 it also ships a charts-facing k-NN spatial index
> (`createSpatialIndex`) that any consumer can inject as a `SpatialIndexFactory`.

## Surface area

ONE class, ONE method, FOUR public properties. That's the entire API.

```ts
class DelaunayTriangulator {
  constructor(maxPoints: number);                    // allocate the arena once
  triangulate(coords, pointCount: number): number;   // run; returns triangleCount

  readonly maxPoints: number;
  readonly triangles: Int32Array;     // vertex indices, 3 per triangle, valid up to trianglesLen
  readonly halfedges: Int32Array;     // twin half-edge indices (or -1 on the hull), parallel
  readonly trianglesLen: number;      // valid-length cursor; equals triangleCount * 3
}
```

`coords` is flat interleaved `[x0, y0, x1, y1, ...]`. Float32Array, Float64Array,
and plain number[] are all accepted (typed access is faster).

## Canonical usage pattern

```js
import { DelaunayTriangulator } from "@zakkster/lite-delaunay";

// Once: pick the largest input you'll ever see.
const tri = new DelaunayTriangulator(10_000);

// Per frame / per call: zero allocations.
const count = tri.triangulate(coords, n);
for (let k = 0; k < count; k++) {
  const a = tri.triangles[k * 3];
  const b = tri.triangles[k * 3 + 1];
  const c = tri.triangles[k * 3 + 2];
  // (coords[a*2], coords[a*2+1]) is the (x,y) of vertex a
}
```

## Half-edge mesh

`halfedges[i]` is the index of the twin half-edge across the shared edge, or
-1 if the edge is on the convex hull. Triangle for half-edge `i` is
`Math.floor(i / 3)`. Next/prev half-edge in the same triangle:

```js
const next = (i % 3 === 2) ? i - 2 : i + 1;
const prev = (i % 3 === 0) ? i + 2 : i - 1;
```

Endpoints of half-edge `i`: `triangles[i]` (start) and `triangles[next]` (end).

For every `e` where `halfedges[e] !== -1`: `halfedges[halfedges[e]] === e`.

## Winding

Triangles are output in **counter-clockwise winding in math coordinates**
(Y-up). In screen-space (Y-down) this looks clockwise. Same convention as
Mapbox Delaunator.

## Degenerate inputs

Return 0 (do NOT throw, do NOT hang):
- pointCount < 3
- all points coincident
- all points fully collinear

`trianglesLen` is reset to 0 on every call, including degenerate ones -- so
stale state never leaks through.

## Throws

- `new DelaunayTriangulator(x)` with x not a non-negative integer
- `tri.triangulate(coords, n)` with `n > maxPoints`

## What it is NOT

- Not a Voronoi library -- the dual graph is easy to extract from the half-edge
  mesh, but you write that step.
- Not robust against ill-conditioned inputs -- uses fast non-robust f64
  predicates, same as Mapbox Delaunator.
- Not auto-growing -- the arena is fixed at construction. Pick a tight bound.

## Algorithm

Sweepline Delaunay (Liu & Snoeyink 2005), ported from Mapbox Delaunator onto
a static Int32Array arena. O(n log n) average, O(n^2) worst-case on adversarial
cocircular inputs.

## Memory footprint

Approximately **68 × maxPoints + 16 KB**.
- maxPoints = 1 000     -> ~80 KB
- maxPoints = 10 000    -> ~700 KB
- maxPoints = 100 000   -> ~7 MB

## Performance (Node 22, Apple-Silicon-class)

| n       | lite-delaunay ms | Mapbox Delaunator ms |
|--------:|-----------------:|---------------------:|
| 1 000   | 0.55             | 0.54                 |
| 10 000  | 6.82             | 7.04                 |
| 100 000 | 86.8             | 93.6                 |

At parity with the reference at typical sizes (1k-10k); ~5-10% ahead at
very large N (50k+); ~1.4× ahead at small N where Delaunator's per-call
allocation dominates. The win is not raw throughput -- it is zero per-call
allocation. Heap delta < 1 KB across 10 000 repeated triangulate() calls
under --expose-gc. Delaunator allocates ~50 KB at small N (output arrays)
which dominates its cost when work is microseconds; that overhead amortizes
away as N grows.

## Common follow-up: Voronoi from the dual

As of v1.2.0 this circumcenter + cell-walk recipe is BUILT IN and hardened
(near-degenerate circumcenters fail closed to the triangle centroid, hull cells
are bbox-clipped, zero allocation) -- see `createCellIndex` below. The manual
recipe stays here for consumers who want the raw dual rather than clipped cells.

```js
// Per-triangle circumcenter scratch -- also allocate once.
const cxArr = new Float32Array(tri.maxTriangles);
const cyArr = new Float32Array(tri.maxTriangles);

// After triangulate():
for (let k = 0; k < count; k++) {
  const a = tri.triangles[k * 3], b = tri.triangles[k * 3 + 1], c = tri.triangles[k * 3 + 2];
  const ax = coords[a*2], ay = coords[a*2+1];
  const bx = coords[b*2], by = coords[b*2+1];
  const cx_ = coords[c*2], cy_ = coords[c*2+1];
  const dx = bx - ax, dy = by - ay, ex = cx_ - ax, ey = cy_ - ay;
  const bl = dx*dx + dy*dy, cl = ex*ex + ey*ey;
  const d  = 0.5 / (dx*ey - dy*ex);
  cxArr[k] = ax + (ey*bl - dy*cl) * d;
  cyArr[k] = ay + (dx*cl - ex*bl) * d;
}
// Voronoi cell of point p = polygon of circumcenters of triangles incident to p,
// walked via the half-edges around p.
```

## Spatial index (v1.1.0)

A second export, `createSpatialIndex`, is the charts-facing capability: a pooled,
zero-allocation k-nearest-neighbour query over a fixed set of pixel coordinates.
It is what `@zakkster/lite-charts` injects to hit-test dense bubble/scatter point
clouds. Implementation is a uniform grid; `triangulate()` is NOT involved.

```ts
const createSpatialIndex: (maxPoints: number) => SpatialIndexFactory;

type SpatialIndexFactory = (pxs, pys, n) => SpatialIndex;

interface SpatialIndex {
  // up to k nearest to (qx, qy) by squared pixel distance, filtered to
  // d <= maxDistSq. Writes ORIGINAL indices + SQUARED distances into the
  // caller-owned outIndices/outDistSq (length >= k), nearest-first. Returns
  // the count written (0..k). k is clamped to 8. Zero allocation.
  findNearest(qx, qy, k, maxDistSq, outIndices, outDistSq): number;
  dispose(): void;
}
```

### Canonical usage: wiring into a lite-charts config

```js
import { createSpatialIndex } from "@zakkster/lite-delaunay";

const chart = createBubbleChart({
  // one factory; the chart builds one index per series and disposes them
  // as data changes. maxPoints must be >= the largest series point count.
  spatialIndex: createSpatialIndex(20_000),
  // ...
});
```

The chart calls `factory(pxs, pys, n)` at extract time (rebuild on data change),
disposes the previous index first, and per hover calls `findNearest`, then
post-filters the k results by disc containment (`hitDistSq[j] <= r*r`) and
smallest-radius tie-break. Containment is INCLUSIVE on both sides, so the index
never hides a hit the linear scan would have found.

### NaN semantics

`pxs` / `pys` are `Float32Array`s that legitimately contain `NaN` (log-scale
projections, missing data). Build compacts ONLY finite points, so `findNearest`
can never return a NaN point. A non-finite query `(qx, qy)` returns `0` -- fail
closed, never a guess.

### Pool / dispose semantics

One factory serves MANY concurrent live handles (a multi-series chart builds one
per series, disposes them independently, rebuilds lazily). Each build acquires a
free pooled slot; each `dispose()` returns it. A new slot is allocated only at a
new concurrent high-water mark. A build allocates exactly one small handle
facade (~48 B, young-gen, minor-GC-collectible); all arenas, grids and scratch
are pooled -- 0 B beyond the facade -- and `findNearest` is 0 B/query. Never
0 B/rebuild.

The facade carries a generation stamp over its pooled slot: `findNearest` and
`dispose` on a disposed handle THROW; double-dispose throws; and a STALE handle
whose slot was rebuilt for another series THROWS rather than silently returning
the new build's points. (With object-reused handles a stale ref is
byte-indistinguishable from a fresh one, so fail-closed forces the fresh facade
per build -- the trade is one ~48 B object, never a wrong answer.)

Degenerate input (all-coincident / all-collinear) is answered correctly by the
grid (it degrades to a 1-cell linear scan) -- never wrong, maybe slow.

### Memory

Per live slot: approximately `24 * maxPoints` bytes plus the grid-cell arrays
(`~ maxPoints` cells). Total peak scales with the concurrent high-water mark of
live handles, not the number of rebuilds. Each build additionally allocates one
~48 B facade (minor-GC-collectible); the torture gate proves 2000 rebuild cycles
cause zero MAJOR GC.

### Throws

- `createSpatialIndex(x)` with x not a non-negative integer
- `factory(pxs, pys, n)` with `n > maxPoints`, `n` not a non-negative integer,
  missing `pxs`/`pys`, or arrays shorter than `n`
- `findNearest` / `dispose` on a disposed handle; double-dispose

## Cell index (v1.2.0)

A third export, `createCellIndex`, is the charts-facing Voronoi-cell capability:
a pooled, zero-allocation query that writes a site's Voronoi polygon, CLIPPED to
a caller-supplied axis-aligned bbox, into a caller-owned buffer. It is what
`@zakkster/lite-charts` injects to draw a cell tessellation over a projected
scatter. Unlike `createSpatialIndex` (a uniform grid), this DOES triangulate:
it builds the Delaunay mesh and precomputes every circumcenter once at build
time, then `cell(i, ...)` walks the half-edges around site `i`.

```ts
const createCellIndex: (maxPoints: number) => CellIndexFactory;

type CellIndexFactory = (pxs, pys, n) => CellIndex;   // Float32Array, NaN legal

interface CellIndex {
  // Write site i's Voronoi polygon, CLIPPED to the bbox, into the caller-owned
  // interleaved outXY [x0,y0,x1,y1,...]. i is the ORIGINAL point index. Returns
  // the vertex count written (0, or 3..outXY.length/2). Every returned polygon
  // is finite, convex, closed (last vertex implicitly connects to first) and
  // fully inside-or-on the bbox -- hull cells are clipped, never flagged.
  // Zero allocation per call.
  //   0 => no cell: i was a non-finite point; the build was degenerate
  //        (fewer than 3 finite points, or collinear/coincident); i lost the
  //        EPSILON dedup (a duplicate that owns no mesh vertex); or the cell
  //        does not intersect the bbox.
  // THROWS (never truncates) if the clipped cell needs more vertices than outXY
  // can hold, if i is not an integer in [0, n), if the bbox is non-finite or
  // not strictly ordered (bx0 < bx1, by0 < by1), or if the handle is disposed.
  cell(i, bx0, by0, bx1, by1, outXY): number;
  dispose(): void;
}
```

### Sizing rule

A bbox-clipped Voronoi cell of an INTERIOR site has at most `degree + 4`
vertices, and of a HULL site at most `degree + 5`. A caller-owned buffer of
`2 * 64` floats (64 vertices) covers every non-adversarial cloud; if a clipped
cell needs more, `cell()` THROWS rather than truncating -- the loud escape.

### Canonical usage: wiring into a lite-charts config

```js
import { createCellIndex } from "@zakkster/lite-delaunay";

const chart = createScatterChart({
  data,
  // all-or-nothing opt-in; the chart rebuilds the index with the projection
  // (Voronoi is not affine-invariant under anisotropic scaling) and disposes
  // the previous one on every data / scale change.
  cells: { index: createCellIndex(20_000), colorKey: 'zone' },
});
```

Cells are PIXEL-space, rebuilt with the projection. The chart calls
`factory(pxs, pys, n)` at extract time, then per frame walks each visible
`cell(i, bx0, by0, bx1, by1, outXY)` at 0 B, filling from a per-point color
accessor. Charts passes the plot bounds as the bbox, so every cell it receives
is finite and closed, or absent.

### Fail-closed list

- A non-finite input point (`NaN`/`Infinity`) is compacted out at build; its
  `cell(i)` returns `0`.
- Near-degenerate circumcenters (denominator ~ 0) fail closed to the triangle
  centroid -- no `Infinity`/`NaN` vertex is ever stored.
- Degenerate build (fewer than 3 finite points, or all-collinear/coincident so
  the triangulation is empty): every `cell(i)` returns `0`.
- An exact/near-duplicate that lost the EPSILON dedup owns no mesh cell; exactly
  one of a set of duplicates returns the polygon, the rest return `0`.
- Hull sites (unbounded in the true diagram) are closed by three synthetic far
  points that provably fall outside the bbox, so the clip yields
  cell-intersect-bbox exactly -- the far-fan is invisible to the caller.

### Pool / dispose semantics

Identical to `createSpatialIndex`: one factory serves many concurrent live
handles, each build acquires a pooled slot and each `dispose()` returns it, a
new slot is allocated only at a new concurrent high-water mark, and a build
allocates exactly one small handle facade (~48 B, minor-GC-collectible) -- 0 B
beyond it, and `cell()` is 0 B/query. The facade carries a generation stamp:
using or double-disposing a disposed handle THROWS, and a stale handle onto a
rebuilt slot THROWS rather than returning the new build's cells.

### Throws

- `createCellIndex(x)` with x not a non-negative integer
- `factory(pxs, pys, n)` with `n > maxPoints`, `n` not a non-negative integer,
  missing `pxs`/`pys`, or arrays shorter than `n`
- `cell(i, ...)` with `i` not an integer in `[0, n)`, a non-finite or
  non-strictly-ordered bbox, an `outXY` too small for the clipped cell, or on a
  disposed handle; `dispose` double-dispose

## Anti-patterns to avoid

- **Do not allocate the triangulator per frame.** That defeats the entire
  point. Construct once at init, reuse forever.
- **Do not read `triangles` past `trianglesLen`.** Indices past that point are
  leftover bytes from previous calls.
- **Do not assume `triangles.length === trianglesLen`.** `triangles.length` is
  the arena capacity (3 × maxTriangles); `trianglesLen` is the valid prefix.
- **Do not pad coords with sentinels** to handle "fewer points this frame".
  Just pass the actual `pointCount`; the arena handles partial usage fine.
